config.title: Berlin Weekend with a Friday Night Arrival - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers for making a late Friday arrival useful without sacrificing Saturday.

items.q: What should I do if I arrive in Berlin on Friday night?
items.a: Treat Friday as an arrival evening rather than a sightseeing test. Make one useful transfer to your hotel, eat close by if you need to, and leave the first major Berlin decision for Saturday morning. The aim is to protect the first clear hour of the weekend rather than to make up for a delayed journey.

items.q: How do I get from BER Airport to central Berlin at night?
items.a: The rail station for BER Terminals 1 and 2 is directly below Terminal 1. Check the official airport rail guide and the live BVG connection search immediately before travelling, because your best FEX, S-Bahn or other connection depends on the actual time and disruption. A trip from BER to central Berlin needs the ABC fare zone.

items.q: Does the U-Bahn run all night on Friday in Berlin?
items.a: Friday night into Saturday falls within Berlin's continuous weekend U-Bahn pattern. That does not replace a live route check: engineering work, delays and the practical connection from your exact station can change, so use the BVG journey planner before you leave.

items.q: Should I go sightseeing after arriving at Berlin Hauptbahnhof?
items.a: Only if it is genuinely close to where you are sleeping and the evening still feels easy. Hauptbahnhof is central, but adding a second cross-city move after checking in often costs more energy than it gives back. Hotel, a nearby meal and Saturday's starting point are usually the better order.

items.q: How should I start Saturday after a late Berlin arrival?
items.a: Choose one real area before you leave the hotel. Alexanderplatz, the World Clock and the walk toward Museum Island work as an east-central start; Hauptbahnhof, the river and the Brandenburg Gate side work as a western-central start. Keep one current booking or priority in view, then let the rest of the day stay flexible.
